newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil makes hydrocarbon find near Yme oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Statoil makes hydrocarbon find near Yme oilfield.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had found hydrocarbons in an exploration well on the Gamma Southeast segment of block 9/2, which embraces the North Sea Yme oilfield.
The well was one of three in an exploration programme targeting promising prospects near the main Yme Gamma West field, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
"The find is small but interesting with an eye to other prospects in the area," said staff engineer Odd Apeland.
Data were being evaluated for possible conversion of the well, which has been temporarily abandoned, from exploration to production.
The next well in the programme will be drilled on the Beta West prospect and is likely to be spudded in the first quarter 1997. A third well will target the Epsilon prospect, Statoil said.

Two Yme reservoirs -- Gamma West and the Beta East satellite -- are producing around 35,000 barrels per day (bpd). Peak output at the two is normally around 50,000 bpd but has been reduced since early September due to a gas compressor breakdown.
Overall recoverable reserves are currently put at around 66 million barrels of oil.
